body:
The generator's hand-written reference table gave MG.2.3 the meaning of MG.2.4, GV.1.2 the meaning of GV.2.1 and MP.5.2 the meaning of MG.1.3, so the rationales written for those items describe another subcategory.

Each MG.2.3 item was classified by what its rationale says:
- 242 that call for disengaging, quarantining or superseding the system now cite MG.2.4
- 263 that describe a planned risk response or runtime treatment cite MG.1.3
- 51 about responding to a previously unknown risk stay on MG.2.3
All 25 GV.1.2 items describe accountability roles and now cite GV.2.1. No rule cited MP.5.2.

scripts/expand-nist-mapping.ts now builds its reference from data/compliance-frameworks/nist_ai_rmf.json, the list CI validates against, and drops the paragraph steering it to GenAI Profile mappings that no rule carries.

How this was checked:
- Parsed before and after, 511 files differ only inside compliance.nist_ai_rmf, and only in the subcategory and the ID written in its own rationale. Strength and the rest of each rationale are unchanged; no rule cites a subcategory twice.
- Local runs: validate, validate:compliance, audit:mappings --require-full, both crosswalk --check. check-rules-safety was stopped locally after about 3 hours on slow rules; see the comment below for why it cannot change for a compliance-only diff. validate.yml only runs on PRs into main, so CI runs it once this PR targets main.

The classification is by keyword, so it needs a human check. A 53-item random sample (10%) with the official statement of each subcategory is ready for a second reviewer; it will be posted as a comment. Please do not merge before that review.

Not in this PR: rationales that cite a correct ID for the wrong reason (for example ATR-2026-00118 cites GV.6.1 for human oversight). Those need a rule-by-rule review.
title: fix(rules): NIST AI RMF mappings cite the subcategory their rationale describes
head: fix/mapping-nist
display_title: fix(rules): NIST AI RMF mappings cite the subcategory their rationale describes
